subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Archimedes' Screw: Lifting Water Uphill
description: A 60-second lesson on Archimedes' Screw: Lifting Water Uphill.

hook.text: Turn a screw inside a tube and water climbs upward. It defies intuition.

buildup.text: A helical blade inside a tilted tube traps water in pockets as it turns.

discovery.text: Each turn lifts the trapped water one pitch higher. Slow but reliable.

twist.text: The design is 2,300 years old and still used in modern water treatment plants.

climax.text: It handles debris, fish, and sewage without clogging — pumps can't match that.

punchline.text: Archimedes' screw still pumps water. Age hasn't improved on it.

quiz.question: Why is the Archimedes screw still used today?
options: It's the most energy-efficient pump available
It handles debris and solids without clogging, unlike most pumps
It can lift water to any height without limit
